name: Planck time
label: 5.4×10⁻⁴⁴ s
summary: Earliest moment current physics can describe. Gravity is thought to split from a single unified force; spacetime behaves classically from here on.

name: Strong force separates
label: ~10⁻³⁶ s
summary: End of grand unification: the strong nuclear force splits from the electroweak force.
range_note: Depends on the unknown grand-unification energy scale; widened.

name: Cosmic inflation
label: ~10⁻³⁶–10⁻³² s
summary: Space expands by at least a factor of 10²⁶. Quantum fluctuations are stretched into the density ripples that later seed galaxies.
range_note: Energy scale of inflation is only bounded from above; timing is model-dependent.

sources.label: Planck 2018 results X: constraints on inflation

name: Reheating fills space with particles
label: ~10⁻³² s
summary: Inflation ends; the inflaton field's energy converts into a hot soup of particles and radiation.
range_note: Reheating temperature is unknown over many orders of magnitude; widened.

name: Matter beats antimatter
label: by ~10⁻¹² s
summary: Baryogenesis leaves a tiny excess of matter — about one extra particle per billion pairs. Why is still unsolved.
range_note: Mechanism unknown; could occur any time between reheating and the electroweak transition.

sources.label: Canetti, Drewes & Shaposhnikov 2012, Matter and antimatter in the universe

name: Higgs field switches on
label: ~10⁻¹² s
summary: Electroweak symmetry breaking: electromagnetism and the weak force separate; quarks, electrons and W/Z bosons gain mass.

sources.label: D'Onofrio & Rummukainen 2016, Standard Model cross-over on the lattice

name: Dark matter freezes out
label: ~10⁻⁸ s (if WIMP)
summary: If dark matter is a heavy particle, its abundance locks in here. Its identity is still unknown.
range_note: Only meaningful for thermal-relic dark matter; the mass is unknown.

name: Quarks bind into protons and neutrons
label: ~1 µs
summary: Quark–gluon plasma cools enough for quarks to be confined inside hadrons.

name: Protons and antiprotons annihilate
label: ~1 ms
summary: Nearly all hadrons annihilate with their antimatter partners, leaving the small matter excess behind.

name: Neutrinos decouple
label: ~1 s
summary: Neutrinos stop interacting and stream freely — the cosmic neutrino background.

name: Electrons and positrons annihilate
label: ~10 s
summary: Most electrons annihilate with positrons, heating the photons; the leftover electrons are all we have today.

name: First nuclei: H, He, Li
label: 3–20 min
summary: Big Bang nucleosynthesis: about 75% hydrogen, 25% helium by mass, a trace of lithium. Every other element comes later.

sources.label: Fields, Olive, Yeh & Young 2020, BBN after Planck

name: Matter starts to dominate
label: ~50,000 yr
summary: Matter (mostly dark matter) outweighs radiation; dark-matter clumps begin to grow, building the scaffolding for galaxies.

name: Atoms form; CMB released
label: ~380,000 yr
summary: Recombination: electrons join nuclei, the universe turns transparent, and the light we now see as the cosmic microwave background escapes.

name: Dark ages begin
label: ~380,000 yr
summary: No stars yet — only cooling neutral gas and growing dark-matter halos.

sources.label: Chronology of the universe: Dark Ages (Wikipedia)

name: First stars ignite
label: ~100–200 Myr
summary: Massive Population III stars form in the first gas clouds — the first stellar nebulae.

sources.label: Bromm 2013, Formation of the first stars

name: First heavy elements forged
label: ~200 Myr
summary: First stars fuse carbon, oxygen and iron, then explode as supernovae, seeding space with heavier elements.

name: Earliest galaxies seen
label: ~290 Myr
summary: The most distant confirmed galaxies, observed by the James Webb Space Telescope.

name: First supermassive black holes
label: ~400–700 Myr
summary: Black holes millions of times the Sun's mass already power quasars and active galaxies.

sources.label: Bogdán et al. 2023, an X-ray quasar at z ≈ 10 (UHZ1)
Wang et al. 2021, a luminous quasar at z = 7.64

name: Gold and uranium from neutron-star mergers
label: ~0.5 Gyr onward
summary: Rapid neutron capture in mergers and rare supernovae makes the heaviest elements.

sources.label: Kasen et al. 2017, r-process in the GW170817 kilonova

name: Milky Way begins assembling
label: ~0.6 Gyr
summary: Our galaxy's oldest stars date from here; it grows by swallowing smaller galaxies.

sources.label: Xiang & Rix 2022, a time-resolved picture of our Milky Way

name: Reionization complete
label: ~1 Gyr
summary: Ultraviolet light from stars and quasars has ionized nearly all the hydrogen between galaxies.

sources.label: Bosman et al. 2022, end of reionization from quasar spectra

name: Cosmic noon
label: ~3.5 Gyr
summary: Peak rate of star formation in the universe's history.

name: Expansion starts accelerating
label: ~7.7 Gyr
summary: Dark energy's push overtakes gravity's pull and cosmic expansion begins to speed up.

sources.label: Riess et al. 1998, accelerating universe from supernovae
Perlmutter et al. 1999, Ω and Λ from 42 supernovae

name: Solar nebula collapses; Sun forms
label: 4.6 Gyr ago
summary: A cloud of gas and dust, enriched by earlier stars, collapses into the Sun and a planet-forming disk.

sources.label: Connelly et al. 2012, absolute chronology of the solar protoplanetary disk

name: Earth forms
label: 4.54 Gyr ago
summary: Rocky material in the disk accretes into Earth.

name: Moon-forming impact
label: ~4.5 Gyr ago
summary: A Mars-sized body strikes the young Earth; the debris coalesces into the Moon.

name: First oceans
label: ~4.4 Gyr ago
summary: Zircon crystals show liquid water on Earth within ~150 million years of its formation.

sources.label: Wilde et al. 2001, evidence for oceans 4.4 Gyr ago

name: Earliest life
label: ~3.8 Gyr ago
summary: Single-celled microbes appear in Earth's oceans.

name: Dark energy dominates
label: ~3.5 Gyr ago
summary: Dark energy becomes the largest component of the universe's energy budget.

name: Great Oxidation Event
label: ~2.4 Gyr ago
summary: Photosynthesizing cyanobacteria fill the atmosphere with oxygen.

name: Complex cells (eukaryotes)
label: ~1.8 Gyr ago
summary: Cells with nuclei and mitochondria arise, likely from one microbe engulfing another.

name: Cambrian explosion
label: 538 Myr ago
summary: Most major animal groups appear in the fossil record.

name: Dinosaurs go extinct
label: 66 Myr ago
summary: An asteroid impact ends the age of dinosaurs and opens the way for mammals.

sources.label: Renne et al. 2013, time scales around the K–Pg boundary

name: Homo sapiens
label: ~300,000 yr ago
summary: Anatomically modern humans appear in Africa.

sources.label: Hublin et al. 2017, Jebel Irhoud Homo sapiens

name: Now
label: 13.8 billion years
summary: Today: about 5% ordinary matter, 27% dark matter, 68% dark energy.
